HOW TO READ THIS COAST

A continuous view.
Traceable data.

Monterey to Point Conception has continuous NOAA coastal relief model context at roughly 30-metre native spacing. The Southern California version 2 model has a 2013 edition and mixed historical inputs. NOAA ETOPO 2022 supplies the wider and deeper ocean backdrop at about 400–500 metres. Both provide modeled context; precise soundings and underwater photography require separate sources. Dated USGS 3DEP bare-earth elevation covers the land across the corridor; its export/display spacing does not establish native lidar accuracy.

Morro Bay’s estuary uses measured NOAA topographic and bathymetric lidar collected June 14, 2022. The original DEM has 1-metre spacing and retains its native missing-data mask. Optical lidar does not resolve every deep or turbid channel; chart estimates or regional context remain separately identifiable in those gaps. Nearby display meshes refine to 4 and 2 metres. The shoreline and channels belong to the same NAVD88 / GEOID12B elevation system. The published 0.052-metre accuracy result applies to tested open land, not every underwater environment. Original product reuse is permitted by the publisher’s No Limit Public License.

USGS survey bathymetry supplies the detailed nearshore seafloor. NOAA chart soundings and depth bands provide labeled estimates in supported gaps. The offshore nominal survey depths, chart reference, NAVD88 land, coastal-model sea level and ETOPO EGM2008 have not been reconciled to a common vertical datum. Broad terrain is context where fine measurements are absent. Source coverage colors and click readings identify the actual source used. Inspection retains original nearest displayed sample values. Native survey and lidar heights remain unchanged within a tile. Coarse land, chart and model context receives bounded presentation filtering and joins nearby fine support within a 32-metre band; this changes displayed context only and adds no measurements. Unsupported interiors retain their original coarse source identity. At streaming boundaries, a separate 256 m display band meets the surrounding parent or neighboring tile surface; displayed heights there can differ more. Clicked measurements retain the original source values. Visual shading, smoothing and continuous triangles do not increase scientific resolution. Closed tile borders use surface joins that avoid deep curtain skirts. Water and shoreline coloring follow the displayed surface; source inspection still returns original unblended samples. Contour lines fade across mixed-source joins to avoid switching depth intervals within a triangle. Rendering seams are covered without adding inspectable measurements.

Water is an illustrative +0.8-metre surface, not a tide prediction or observation. It shows submerged channels and flats while allowing the bottom to remain visible. NOAA lidar readings show native elevation; offshore readings retain nominal depth. The relief slider emphasizes seabed height for readability; land remains true scale. These views must not be used for navigation.

Both perspectives share exactly the same terrain, reef outlines, target species, rankings, source evidence, water, currents and selections. The toggle changes the camera only. Dated USGS / USDA NAIP aerial imagery drapes the land. Close views load bounded 2048-pixel detail tiles at 2-metre display spacing; this is display sampling, not positional accuracy. Source catalog dates vary within each footprint and are preserved in the imagery receipts. It is not live imagery. The original overview imagery supplies a per-pixel fallback, and detail texture edges blend across 96 metres; missing imagery remains shaded terrain context. The original wide imagery remains the fallback; outside imagery coverage, shaded elevation supplies geographic context.

At broad zoom, colored areas fill only admitted habitat polygons and preserve their holes. At closer zoom, compact pins identify individual reefs; selecting one opens original depth, rank and source evidence. These display changes do not create new habitat footprints. All 4,560 reef context outlines originate from the commercially eligible, whole-polygon screened SkipperCast publication. Context outlines use a 6-metre rendering simplification; 12 outlines retain their original geometry where that simplification would be invalid. Curated detailed outlines retain their full geometry. Original species fit, terrain grade, score, survey dates, support and screening expiry remain unchanged. Rankings describe physical habitat, not fish abundance or catch probability. The release now includes 904 Monterey/Carmel/Point Sur and 788 Arguello/Conception habitat candidates, alongside the original SLO packages. Survey gaps through parts of Big Sur and the northern Arguello reach have no inferred fishing candidates. Northern Monterey beyond the reviewed restriction scope remains held. Historical surveys do not establish present fish or current season, gear, route, launch-day or vessel-security clearance. Full context is withdrawn when its producer binding changes. A newer, independently reviewed curated edition can still upgrade the map while full context is rebuilt. All reefs are withdrawn if rights or screening gates fail. Halibut and surfperch show original sandy-shore context only, with no inferred offshore habitat scores. Historical access facts do not establish current legal access.

Surface currents are shown only where a reviewed current product passes its original time limits. Vector blending stays within complete adjacent wet source cells. More display arrows do not add observations or source resolution. No currents are invented for uncovered coast.
